what_happened: Job 20261113-194336-scfc (code job: escalate the planner's model and effort when planning thrashes) failed in planning, before any code was written. The critic said in round 1 that the reading misread the request, and the plan still needed revising after round 5 of 5. The reading mapped "improve the model" to the existing hard_producer_model and hard_producer_effort keys. In this repo, [job_plan] mode = "hard" plans only hard readings, and those already use hard_producer_model. hard_producer_effort ("high") also equals the planner's verifier_effort ("high"). So the change would do nothing here. Two major findings remained. First, the escalation could lower the planner's effort or model, because those keys are tuned for the producer and not the planner. Second, the plan misstated the effect in this repo. One minor finding: the criterion asks for model and effort from Models::producer_setting, but the plan takes only the model from it. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Nothing checks a reading's mapping of a request onto existing config keys against the live config and the code that reads them. The reading took the existing hard_producer_* keys as "a stronger model" for the planner without checking how athena.toml and reading.rs already use them: the planner runs in hard mode on a model that already has that setting, and the keys are tuned against the producer. The plan then built on that premise. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no mechanical repair step, so two major findings that survive round 5 lose all planning spend.
other_causes: The plan's claim about its effect in this repo was never checked against the repo's own config values.
The new rule sets the planner's effort and model from keys meant for another role, with no never-lower guard.
open_hypotheses: Whether a separate planner escalation key would have satisfied the owner's intent cannot be told from the fields given.
Whether the critic's round-1 misread finding could have been fixed in an early round, or the planner ignored it, cannot be told from the stored fields.
contradictions: The owner accepted the reading, which points to the premise being a stated intent and not a misreading by Athena alone.
The earlier case in this class was a field with the wrong meaning. Here the keys have the right meaning but the wrong role and no effect, so the fit is only partial.
prevention: Before a reading is accepted, run a step that resolves each config key or field it reuses against the live athena.toml and the code that reads it. It should report the effective value for each role and whether the change would alter behavior in this repo. A reading whose change is a no-op, or could lower a setting, should be sent back or flagged to the owner at reading time. Planning should also get a repair round for a mechanical finding such as "add an optional key".
proposed_request: Escalate the planner on revision rounds, as one change. When the planning critic returns "needs revising", the planner's next round should use a model and effort at least as strong as its current ones. Add optional keys planner_revision_model and planner_revision_effort under [models], and use them only when they are set and not weaker than the current planner setting. Do not reuse hard_producer_model or hard_producer_effort. Resolve the keys against athena.toml and reading.rs first. State in the plan the effective planner model and effort in this repo with and without the change. Acceptance: (1) with the keys set, a revision round runs with the stronger model and effort, shown through Athena::go with the fake agent; (2) a key that would lower the model or effort is ignored; (3) with the keys unset, behavior is unchanged; (4) the changelog entry says what the keys do in this repo. Deliverables: the config.rs change, the planning.rs change, tests, the athena.toml entry and CHANGELOG.md.
